Following the ongoing AirPods Pro 3 25% off deal and last week's $120 discount on AirPods Max 2, today's 9to5Toys midday headline once again reports Amazon has dropped AirTag 2 to a new historical low, with the four-pack now selling for $80 (or $20 each). Additionally, the Apple M5 MacBook Pro with 24GB/1TB is discounted by $320, while the 2TB M5 Pro gets an additional $500 off; also don't miss Anker's brand-new SmartTrack "Find My" wallet card hitting an Amazon all-time low of $25, as well as the LG 32-inch 6K Thunderbolt 5 monitor, which is a whopping $2,200 cheaper than the Apple Studio Display XDR (historical new low). Read on for details.

The latest AirPods Pro 3 maintains its 25% off deal, with broad expectations the next generation will arrive in 2027

  • AirPods Pro 3 $190 (original price $249)
  • AirPods Max 2 $429 (original price $549)
  • AirPods 4 $99 (original price $129)

Wow! AirTag 2 receives another discount, four-pack hits historical new low of $80 (or $20 each)

Great news everyone! Amazon has just dropped the Apple 2026 AirTag 2 four-pack to a new historical low, at just $20 per tracker.

Amazon is now offering the AirTag 2 four-pack at $79.99, with free shipping.

Last week we had been tracking this official pack's price at $89.99, then Amazon cut it to $85 yesterday, and the new week brings further reductions. Priced at $99, so roughly 20% off, it doesn't sound like a lot, but it's a fairly significant discount for the latest AirTag 2.

On average, this pack works out to about $20 per AirTag, the lowest price since its launch earlier this year.

The single AirTag 2 link is still maintaining last week's Prime member free shipping low of $24, but the four-pack has (once again) dropped even lower.

Incidentally, the $20 per unit price here matches the best open-box pricing we saw at Best Buy last week.

Apple 24GB/1TB M5 MacBook Pro discounted by $320, 2TB M5 Pro discounted by $500

Beyond the ongoing AirPods Pro 3 25% off deal and the AirTag 2 tracking new low, as we head into the new week we're also bringing you several notable MacBook Pro series deals. Amazon still has the 2TB M5 Pro at $500 off, and we've also spotted a more affordable M5 MacBook Pro 24GB configuration with $300 off. Details below.

If you've had your eye on the more powerful M5 Pro, Amazon's $500-off model is definitely worth considering. But if the more affordable M5 suits you better, B&H's 14-inch 24GB/1TB configuration is also quite attractive:

B&H has once again dropped the 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro with 24GB RAM and 1TB internal storage to $1,899, with free shipping.

  • 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro 24GB/1TB $1,899 (original price $2,219)
  • With upgraded 96W Apple charger included

On this $2,199 machine, B&H is also throwing in the official 96W Apple charger—which would cost an extra $20 if added on Apple's website.

Amazon currently has the same configuration MacBook Pro at $2,049, but only with the standard 70W charger.

All things considered, B&H's deal saves you $320, matching the previously mentioned discount level, and well below Amazon's current price.

However, as mentioned earlier, Amazon still has a notable discount on the 14-inch M5 Pro MacBook Pro 24GB/2TB, down to $2,699—$500 below the $3,199 MSRP, and this deal may not last long.

Anker's new SmartTrack "Find My" wallet card (supports iOS or Android) hits Amazon all-time low of $25

Anker recently launched its new SmartTrack "Find My" wallet card—the first product to simultaneously support both Apple's tracking platform and Google Find Hub—now available on Amazon at a new historical low of $25 with Prime member free shipping.

This product only first appeared on Amazon last month at $35, with a slight $5 reduction by month's end, and now sees its first significant discount, hitting an Amazon all-time low.

That's nearly 30% off, matching the best deals on other wallet tracker cards this year.

I'm personally a super fan of the Nomad tracking card—the standard version starts at $35, and the Pro version with 16-month battery life sells for $45—but regardless of which you choose, I think everyone should put one in their wallet or cardholder. I never leave the house without one.

Anker's latest SmartTrack Card E40 covers all the most important features, including wireless charging, while supporting both Apple's "Find My" platform or Google Find Hub. At just 1.7mm thin, with an alarm volume of up to 80 decibels for easy nearby locating—of course you can also add it to the "Find My" and Find Hub apps to check its location on a map.

Organize your desk with this Anker smart power strip, now reduced to $58

LG 32-inch 6K Thunderbolt 5 monitor hits new lowest price, a whopping $2,200 cheaper than Studio Display XDR

We've just spotted a deal at B&H dropping the LG 32-inch UltraFine evo 6K monitor to $1,099.99, with free shipping. This monitor is normally priced at $2,000, peaking around $1,597 in recent months. Today's deal matches Amazon's earlier this month historical new low, and that price is still in effect. LG's official website today also lists it at $1,100, so even if a particular retailer sells out, you still have plenty of options. At this price, the UltraFine evo 6K is well below Apple's display offerings. The Studio Display XDR starts at $3,299, meaning the LG 32-inch 6K Thunderbolt 5 monitor is over $2,200 cheaper. Even the standard Studio Display starts at $1,549, so you could save around $500 and get a larger 32-inch 6K screen. Read on for details.

The LG 32-inch UltraFine evo 6K is a high-end workstation monitor designed for creators who want a large, high-resolution screen without upgrading to Apple's more expensive options. Its 6144 x 3456 screen has over 21 million pixels at 224 PPI, providing ample space for editing timelines, full-resolution content, tools, and multiple windows. Color gamut coverage reaches 99.5% Adobe RGB, and it supports VESA DisplayHDR 600 for better highlights and contrast. Connectivity is also very comprehensive, including Thunderbolt 5, DisplayPort 2.1, HDMI, and USB-C. Mac users can also access calibrated color presets via LG's Studio Mode for more consistent creative work. Overall, this 6K monitor is feature-rich, suitable for any user who wants truly expansive screen real estate without paying Apple's display prices.

If you don't want to spend over $1,000 on a new monitor, Woot also has deals on several more affordable Samsung workstation monitors. The M series and other budget models are discounted, with entry prices starting at just $118.

Today's accessory and charging deals:

  • This ultra-thin UGREEN wallet tracker card supports iPhone and Android, now just $20 (historical new low)
  • This compact UGREEN ultra-thin 45W Nexode Air charger is the thinnest in my EDC, now reduced to $27
  • Twelve South AirFly Pro wireless audio transmitter reduced to $40 at Amazon (black or white)
  • Chipolo Google Find Hub wallet card with action button/remote shutter, now $33
  • UGREEN MagFlow 25W Qi2.2 car charger back to $28 (original price $40)
  • Acer metal MagSafe golf cart mount reduced to $20 with Prime member free shipping

Latest wireless Ring Battery Doorbell 4K Pro hits Amazon all-time low, nearly 30% off (wired version also available)

As part of a series of discounts on Fire tablets, Fire TV, and Blink smart home products to close out summer, Amazon is now offering the latest wireless Ring Battery Doorbell 4K Pro at its historical lowest price, and is repeating Prime Day's historical new low on the wired version—both at nearly 70% of retail.

  • Ring Battery Doorbell 4K Pro $180 (original price $250)
  • Ring Wired Doorbell 4K Pro $180 (original price $250)

Although Ring subsequently launched the more affordable Ring Peephole Cam 2K at $100, today we're focusing on several particularly notable deals for its latest Pro series 4K models.

The Ring Wired Doorbell 4K Pro is now back at its Prime Day historical new low, its first appearance since the late June promotional event. In fact, this is only the second time we've tracked this model below $200.

The wireless Ring Battery Doorbell 4K Pro is now seeing its first discount, also hitting a historical new low of $180.

As noted above, both models are priced at $250, or nearly 30% off—the best deals we've found and the lowest prices to date.

The two are largely similar, featuring retina 4K imaging, 10x enhanced zoom, night vision, and wide-angle field of view to give you a clearer picture of what's at your door; the wireless version includes a Quick Release Ultra battery pack for easy charging and simpler installation (no wiring required), while the wired version offers "uninterrupted power, uninterrupted protection."

For more details, you can refer to our product launch coverage from last September.

Best Buy launches new tech deals, NFL Sunday Ticket promotions, and preseason TV deals

Amazon drops $120 off AirPods Max 2 in all five colors (one of the all-time best prices)

This week's major 60th anniversary celebration sale brings one of the all-time best prices for the Apple 2026 AirPods Max 2, with Amazon offering $120 off across all five colors.

Amazon is now dropping the Apple AirPods Max 2 to $429, with free shipping.

Compared to the same-priced $549 previous generation, that's a full $120 saved—the best price for a new unit from a reputable retailer.

Best Buy has dropped the midnight black version to $403.99, with free shipping, in "excellent" open-box condition. Although the price is lower, given the small difference, giving up a new unit isn't really worth it.

Apple has launched a true new generation of AirPods Max this year, unlike the previous generation which only changed colors and added a USB-C port. Unlike the in-ear AirPods lineup, its over-ear product line won't be updated at next month's new product launch event, so this week you can consider picking up what may become Apple's premier over-ear headphones at a $120 discount.

Previously only one promotional event was cheaper than this—Prime Day earlier this year, which was $30 below today's deal price—but inventory was very unstable during that 4-day promotional period.

Amazon selling this 512GB iPad mini at a new low price, $450 off (Renewed Premium)

While iPad Air deals have only just started emerging this week, overall iPad discounts have been weak or nearly nonexistent recently. However, we've just spotted Amazon selling the 512GB iPad mini at a new low price, with a massive $450 discount in top-tier Renewed Premium condition.

Amazon is now dropping the 512GB iPad mini A17—the latest model—to $449, with free shipping.

That means this iPad, priced at $899 from Apple, can now be purchased directly from Amazon for $450 less.

Worth noting: even before price increases, we've never seen this model below $679 in new condition on Amazon.

A reminder that Amazon Renewed Premium models differ from regular Renewed products, and also from "excellent" condition refurbished units. Here are their standards:

  • Screen: If equipped with a screen, absolutely no scratches whatsoever.
  • Body: No visible cosmetic damage (scratches, dents, etc.) when viewed from 12 inches away.
  • Battery: If equipped, battery capacity exceeds 90% of original battery life.
  • Accessories: Original or generic accessories and packaging provided.
  • Guarantee: Renewed Premium products enjoy a 365-day return policy.

Amazon's top-tier Premium Renewed iPhone 17 Pro units now $220 off (matches Prime Day deal)

Although Apple's official certified refurbished store is my first choice for iPhone deals, Apple hasn't yet sold the latest iPhone 17 Pro models there—it looks like we'll have to wait until after the 18 series launches next month. Amazon's top-tier Premium Renewed inventory has now been repriced to Prime Day levels, with new unit pricing reduced by up to $220.

To date, Amazon's top-tier Premium Renewed models are the most cost-effective way to purchase an unlocked iPhone 17 Pro. You not only save hundreds of dollars, but also get a 1-year Amazon Renewed warranty and "over 90% original battery life"—rather than the 90-day warranty and incomparable battery life standards of non-Premium Renewed and Refurbished products.

Now both 1TB and 512GB iPhone 17 Pro models are again reduced by up to $220—the 512GB version is $20 lower than the previously mentioned price:

  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,279 (original new unit price $1,499)
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,279 (original new unit price $1,499)
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,279 (original new unit price $1,499)
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,179 (original new unit price $1,299)
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,179 (original new unit price $1,299)
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,179 (original new unit price $1,299)

As highlighted in yesterday's Apple refurbished store feature, you can get a fully functional iPhone 16 with 1-year Apple warranty starting from $699, or a 1TB 16 Pro Max for $1,269—$330 cheaper than the corresponding 17 Pro Max, and $130 cheaper than the 512GB 17 Pro.

  • Refurbished iPhone 16 from $699 (up to $330 cheaper than the 17 series)
